view.designs.install_prompt: A dismissable notice on the list of the user's designs, offered only when their browser can install this web app (as a home-screen / desktop app). Shown beside a button labelled with view.designs.install.
view.designs.install: The button on that notice which opens the browser's own install dialog. Use the word the language's browsers use for installing a web app.
app.beta: A small badge beside the app's name in the header, marking it as a beta release.
common.end: A toggle button choosing which part of a long document the live preview shows: its end.
common.home: A back button on the About and Privacy pages that returns to the app's main page (the list of designs).
common.start: A toggle button choosing which part of a long document the live preview shows: its start.
common.us_letter: The North American paper size (8.5 × 11 in), offered beside A4.
dialog.account.delete_word: The word the user must type to confirm deleting their account; it is also inserted into dialog.account.delete_confirm as {word}. Use a single word in capitals where the script has them.
dialog.fonts.get_font_step: "Get font" and "Download all" are button names on Google Fonts' website; keep them as that site shows them.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_color_bw: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website, which the user has to find there. Keep it in English as Lulu shows it.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_color_std: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website, which the user has to find there. Keep it in English as Lulu shows it.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_finish_glossy: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website, which the user has to find there. Keep it in English as Lulu shows it.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_finish_matte: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website, which the user has to find there. Keep it in English as Lulu shows it.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_paper_60: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website (60 lb paper). Keep it as Lulu shows it.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_paper_80: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website (80 lb paper). Keep it as Lulu shows it.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_paper_cream: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website, which the user has to find there. Keep it in English as Lulu shows it.
dialog.how_to_print.lulu_paper_white: The exact name of an option on Lulu's English-only website, which the user has to find there. Keep it in English as Lulu shows it.
dialog.phone_preview.keep_editing: Button at the top of the full-screen preview on a phone, closing it to go back to editing the book.
dialog.phone_preview.too_slow: Shown under a spinner in the full-screen preview on a phone, once making the preview on the device took too long: our servers are now making this preview instead, and from now on they also build the user's books (make them into printable PDFs) instead of the device.
display.preview.waiting_online: Progress text under a timer while a book being built has lost its internet connection: its PDF is ready (or must be handed to our servers) and is sent as soon as the device is back online.
display.preview.waiting_previous: Progress text under a timer while a book being built waits for the user's previous build, still being made on their device, to finish first. 'Build' is the act of making the printable PDF.
doc.chapter: The heading printed above each chapter when the 'heading' chapter style is chosen; {n} is the chapter number. Use the word published Bibles in this language use for a chapter, and put {n} where it goes (some languages put the number first or wrap it, e.g. "第{n}章").
doc.copyright.created_with: A bold line at the top of the copyright page; {link} becomes the link "/paper.bible/" (the app's name, styled as a URL).
doc.copyright.customize: Bold text beside a QR code on the copyright page, inviting the reader to scan it to open this book's design, customise it and print their own copy.
doc.copyright.modify: A licensing statement covering the whole book. Translate precisely: anyone may copy it, change it and translate it into other languages.
doc.copyright.public_domain: Says everything in the book other than the listed resources (the creator's own pages) is dedicated to the public domain; {site} is a web address that explains what that means.
doc.copyright.resources: The heading over the list of Bible translations and other works the book includes, each with its license.
doc.copyright.share: A licensing statement covering the whole book. Translate precisely: anyone may copy it and share it (but not change it).
doc.copyright.study_notes: Labels the study-notes row in that list; printed as "<this> — Tyndale House Publishers".
editor.advanced.heading_chapter: An option in the chapter-number style dropdown: each chapter starts with a heading. After the "|" is a sample of that heading for chapter {n} (always 2), so write it the way Bibles in this language print a chapter heading (e.g. "第{n}章").
svc.blueprint.service_home: The chosen printing service when printing at home on your own printer (not a booklet) — shown as a short label in design summaries.
svc.examples.large_print_title: The title printed on the cover of an example large-print edition of the Bible books 1 Kings and 2 Kings. Write the two book names the way published Bibles in this language name them, joined as compactly as the English "1 & 2 Kings".
view.design.preview: Button on a phone that shows the full-screen preview of the book being designed, before it's built (made into a printable PDF).
vuetify.close: Screen-reader label for a close button on an alert or chip.
vuetify.dismiss: Screen-reader label for a button that dismisses a notice.
vuetify.input.appendAction: Screen-reader label for an icon button at the end of a field; {0} is the field's label.
vuetify.input.clear: Screen-reader label for the button that clears a text field; {0} is the field's label.
vuetify.input.prependAction: Screen-reader label for an icon button at the start of a field; {0} is the field's label.
vuetify.loading: Screen-reader label for a loading spinner.
vuetify.noDataText: Shown inside a dropdown list that has no items to choose from.
vuetify.open: Screen-reader label for the button that opens a dropdown list.
wizard.type.coming: Subtitle on a not-yet-available design type card in the new-design wizard. {date} is a short month and year already formatted in the UI language, e.g. "Dec 2026".
display.preview.on_server: Progress text while the preview of a book is being made on our servers rather than on the user's device (followed by "…").
display.preview.refresh: Button in the live preview's toolbar that asks for a fresh preview of the book as it is now. Shown only when previews are made on our servers, which don't update automatically as the user edits.
display.preview.zoom: Tooltip of the preview's zoom button, with the current zoom as a percentage already formatted for the locale (e.g. "150%"). On a computer 100% is the book's printed size; on a phone, the pages filling the screen's width.
display.preview.print_size: Tooltip of a button labelled "1×" in the preview's zoom control, which zooms to the book's printed size (as nearly as the screen allows).
display.preview.fit_width: Tooltip of a button in the preview's zoom control that zooms the pages to fill the width of the preview again.
display.preview.a4_width: Label under a line drawn as wide as a sheet of A4 paper, shown while the zoom control is open, so a real sheet can be held against it.
display.preview.letter_width: Label under a line drawn as wide as a sheet of US Letter paper (8.5 inches; ″ is the inch sign), shown while the zoom control is open.
display.preview.lines_overflow: Warning under the paper-width lines when the window is too narrow to show them at full length.
display.preview.measure_hint: Instructions under the paper-width lines: holding a real sheet of paper against the screen and zooming until the line matches it makes the preview show the book at its true size.
display.preview.measure_note: Shown in parentheses under display.preview.measure_hint, explaining why the zoom usually needs adjusting.
editor.advanced.draw_lines: Label of a toggle choosing the lines drawn on a book's blank pages for the reader to write notes on: None, or the spacing of narrow, medium or wide ruled notebook paper.
editor.advanced.lines_narrow: A toggle button choosing how far apart the handwriting lines on a book's blank pages are, named after the standard rulings of notebook paper (narrow, medium/college, wide ruled). This one: the closest lines, for small handwriting. Use your language's term for narrow ruled paper if it has one.
editor.advanced.lines_medium: A toggle button choosing how far apart the handwriting lines on a book's blank pages are, named after the standard rulings of notebook paper (narrow, medium/college, wide ruled). This one: the middle spacing (college ruled).
editor.advanced.lines_wide: A toggle button choosing how far apart the handwriting lines on a book's blank pages are, named after the standard rulings of notebook paper (narrow, medium/college, wide ruled). This one: the widest lines, for large handwriting.
